cit_fast: Accelerated naturalization after 3 years ("besondere Integrationsleistungen", C1 + special integration), introduced in June 2024, has been ABOLISHED: the bill was passed by the Bundestag on 8.10.2025 (450 for/134 against), the law entered into force on 30.10.2025. The basic period remains 5 years (reduced from 8 in 2024 by the StAG reform) for all categories. For spouses of Germans, usually after 3 years of marriage with 2+ years of residence permit (about 5 years in total, possible reduction to 3 years under § 9 StAG with special language/social integration).
counts_note: Germany has no separate 'digital nomad' visa; the freelancer visa (§21 AufenthG, Freiberufler/self-employment) is usually credited as a work residence permit (full) if issued as a residence permit for self-employment, and not through third jurisdictions. The student period is usually at 50%.
presence: Permanent residence in Germany is required; permitted interruptions are limited (on average no more than ~6 months in a row/up to 10 months over the whole period without risk of interrupting the term), final assessment by the authority at the place of residence (Ausländerbehörde/Einbürgerungsbehörde).
language: German B1 (oral and written) + the 'Leben in Deutschland' test (33 questions on the constitutional order, society, history).
children: Minor children permanently residing in Germany are, as a rule, included in the parent's application (Miteinbürgerung) subject to the residence period requirements (usually a shorter residence period of the child is sufficient, decision under §10 StAG); automatic citizenship by birth in Germany (jus soli) also applies under certain residence conditions of the parent.

cit_fast: Citizenship is granted immediately under the 'Law of Return' to persons of Jewish origin (including grandchildren of a Jew) and their families upon repatriation (aliyah). For everyone else — ordinary naturalization: permanent residence in Israel for at least 3 of the last 5 years with a residence permit (teudat ezrach / residence permit type A/5), plus the intention to live permanently in the country.
counts_note: Israel has no digital nomad visa (n_a); most residence permit routes for persons without the right of aliyah are extremely limited (no separate work-based permanent residence visa for ordinary foreigners outside special categories), which makes naturalisation 'from scratch' through work practically unrealistic without marriage to a citizen or the right of aliyah.
presence: Actual permanent residence in the country during the specified period is required (not formal registration).
language: Basic knowledge of Hebrew (for standard naturalization) and renunciation/loss of foreign citizenship as a condition of the oath in a number of cases.
children: Children of repatriates receive citizenship together with the parent upon aliyah; with ordinary naturalisation of the parent, minor children are, as a rule, included in the application.

cit_fast: 2 years for citizens of Ibero-America, Andorra, the Philippines, Equatorial Guinea, Portugal and Sephardim; 1 year — for marriage to a Spaniard (after 1 year of marriage and living together), birth in Spain, or for refugees.
counts_note: The digital nomad visa (Ley de Startups, since 2023) gives a residence permit which in general counts towards the period for permanent residence/citizenship as ordinary 'legal residence', since it is issued as residencia (not a separate category without qualifying time), but requires confirmation in practice at each renewal.
presence: Continuous and legal residence (residencia continuada y legal) at the time of filing; absences must not interrupt the residence permit.
language: DELE A2 test (Spanish) + CCSE test (Spanish constitution and sociocultural knowledge).
children: Minor children living with the applicant parent generally obtain citizenship together with them on a derivative basis.

cit_fast: No special fast-track routes for ordinary migrants; for citizens of New Zealand and those with special merit to the country the terms may differ. Requirement: 4 years of lawful residence in Australia immediately before applying, of which the last 12 months with a permanent visa (PR), and no more than 12 months of absences in 4 years (no more than 90 days in the last year).
counts_note: Australia has no digital nomad visa as such (n_a); a student visa (subclass 500) counts towards the overall 4-year residence period (full), since the rule counts any legal temporary residence within 4 years, only the last year must be on a permanent visa.
presence: Maximum 12 months of absence in 4 years, maximum 90 days of absence in the last year before applying.
language: There is no separate language test for naturalization, but the citizenship test (Australian Citizenship Test) is conducted in English and indirectly requires knowledge of it.
children: Minor children of permanent residents/citizens, as a rule, apply simultaneously with the parent (on a joint basis), or obtain citizenship by virtue of the parent's permanent residence.

cit_fast: 6 years for special merits (Vorzeigen besonderer Leistungen at the cultural/sporting/economic level) or 6 years if married to an Austrian citizen (with a 5-year continuous joint marriage and 5 years of residence). For refugees/stateless persons — 6 years.
counts_note: Austria has no separate digital nomad visa; the self-employed obtain a 'Selbständige Erwerbstätigkeit' residence permit (usually full counting, but with a high income/investment threshold). Rot-Weiß-Rot Karte plus for other categories is also full.
presence: A primary residence (Hauptwohnsitz) in Austria is required throughout the entire period; long absences interrupt continuity of residence.
language: German level B1 (oral and written) + a test on Austrian history/state structure (Staatsbürgerschaftsprüfung).
children: Minor children are, as a rule, included in the parent's application (Erstreckung der Verleihung) if they live together and meet the general conditions.

cit_fast: Accelerated routes are mainly for ethnic Azerbaijanis/special merits; for ordinary applicants — the general term of from 5 years of permanent residence after obtaining a residence permit/permanent residence.
counts_note: The exact rules for crediting different residence permit categories towards the naturalisation residence period are not fully formalised in open sources; estimate based on Azerbaijan's general migration legislation.
presence: Permanent residence in the territory of the country is required; exact norms for permitted absences not found in open official sources.
language: Knowledge of Azerbaijani at a level sufficient for communication (a specific formalized test is not confirmed in open sources).
children: Minor children, as a rule, acquire citizenship together with the applicant parent under the general procedure of migration law.

cit_fast: Under Argentine law (art. 20 of the Constitution and Law 346) a foreigner can apply for citizenship ('carta de ciudadanía') through a court after 2 years of continuous residence in the country (in practice temporary residence is often enough, not necessarily permanent), which is one of the fastest routes in the world.
counts_note: Argentina generally credits almost any legal form of temporary or permanent residence (residencia temporaria/permanente) towards the 2-year term for citizenship via the court; the 'rentista'/digital nomad visa also usually qualifies if issued as a residencia.
presence: Continuous actual residence in the country for 2 years without long trips abroad is required (short trips are permitted, but a long absence may interrupt the term).
language: There is no formal mandatory language test for naturalization through the court, but Spanish is necessary for the court process/interview.
children: Minor children residing in the country, as a rule, receive citizenship simultaneously with the parent's naturalization or by virtue of continuous residence.

cit_fast: Simplified procedure for ethnic Armenians and spouses of Armenian citizens (sometimes without a residence period requirement); for ordinary applicants — 3 years of permanent residence.
counts_note: A separate residence permit category for freelancers/digital nomads is not officially defined in Armenia; usually the general residence permit is used, which should count towards the 3-year term, but no detailed official clarifications on crediting different types of residence permit were found.
presence: Permanent residence in the country during the specified period is required (details on permitted absences were not found in open official sources in English).
language: Knowledge of Armenian at a level sufficient for integration; a specific formalized exam is not confirmed in open sources.
children: Minor children, as a rule, acquire citizenship together with the parent when the application is filed.

cit_fast: There are few separate fast-track routes; for citizens with 10 years of continuous legal residence naturalisation with lower integration requirements is possible ('naturalisation' through parliament — an extremely rare route). The main route is 'déclaration de nationalité' after 5 years of legal residence with confirmed social/economic/language integration.
counts_note: There is no official digital nomad visa in Belgium; self-employed persons obtain a residence permit on the basis of a professional card (carte professionnelle), which should count as an ordinary legal residence permit (full), but no unambiguous confirmation for digital nomads was found.
presence: Continuous legal residence (résidence légale ininterrompue) for 5 years immediately before filing the declaration is required.
language: One of the three national languages, level A2 (per the current text of the Nationality Code, art. 12bis; level B1 was announced by the "Arizona" government in 2025, but as of 23.06.2026 it is not enshrined in law and not in force), plus proof of social integration (the region's integration course) or 5 years of work experience.
children: Minor children of a foreigner naturalizing in Belgium generally acquire Belgian citizenship automatically together with the parent if living together (art. 12 of the Citizenship Code, 'effect on children': a child under 18 or not emancipated before 18, under the parental authority of this parent and with the main place of residence in Belgium on the date of acquisition; art. 12bis — a declaration by the adult themselves).

cit_fast: For persons of Bulgarian origin — from 3 years of continuous residence (simplified procedure), for spouses of Bulgarian citizens (married for 3+ years) — reduced residence requirements; for investors through the purchase of government bonds — special (accelerated, but politically sensitive) programmes have been suspended and resumed.
counts_note: There is no official digital nomad visa in Bulgaria; a type D visa for self-employed/freelancers is usually counted as an ordinary legal residence permit (full), but no separate confirmation of its counting towards the citizenship residence period was found.
presence: Continuous permanent residence in the territory of Bulgaria for a set period before filing is required (a valid permanent residence).
language: Bulgarian language (oral and written exam), knowledge of the Constitution of Bulgaria.
children: Minor children are, as a rule, included in the applicant parent's naturalisation application.

cit_fast: For spouses of BiH citizens in a marriage of 3 years or more — a shortened residence period (usually from 3 years of permanent residence in marriage); no other fast-track routes identified for typical applicants.
counts_note: Detailed official rules on crediting various types of residence permit towards the total term for naturalisation were not found in open sources in English in sufficient detail.
presence: Continuous residence on a permanent residence permit (stalni boravak) for a set period before filing is required.
language: Knowledge of one of the official languages (Bosnian/Serbian/Croatian) at an everyday level.
children: Minor children are generally included in the parent's naturalization application under the general procedure of migration law.

cit_fast: The shortened term (usually stated as 2 years under Migration Law No. 13.445/2017, art. 65) applies when additional conditions are met: a Brazilian spouse/child, a significant professional/scientific/cultural contribution, investment in production/real estate, or for refugees. The prompt gives a term of 3 years for property owners — additional verification of the exact figure (2 or 3 years) against the current regulation is recommended.
counts_note: The VITEM XIV visa / Brazil's digital nomad visa (since 2022) gives a residence permit, but its counting toward the naturalization period is not formally singled out in open sources — needs clarification with the Polícia Federal.
presence: Permanent residence in Brazil is required; permitted absences are limited (details on specific absence periods not found in sufficient detail).
language: Celpe-Bras test (Portuguese proficiency certificate) is mandatory for naturalisation.
children: Minor children of a foreigner residing in Brazil, as a rule, can obtain citizenship by virtue of permanent residence simultaneously with the parent.

cit_fast: Via the Global Talent visa ILR is possible after only 3 years (for 'exceptional talent') or sooner for 'exceptional promise'; when married to a UK citizen, ILR + naturalisation is possible immediately after obtaining ILR (without the additional 12-month wait required for non-spouses).
counts_note: The UK has no digital nomad visa giving a path to ILR (n_a) — only the temporary Standard Visitor allows remote work without a right of residence/naturalization. The ordinary work visa (Skilled Worker) — full.
presence: No more than 180 days of absence in any rolling 12 months during the qualifying period before applying for ILR and for naturalization.
language: English level B1 (KOELL) + 'Life in the UK' test.
children: Minor children are, as a rule, registered as British citizens by a separate application after the parent obtains ILR/citizenship (registration of the child, not automatic inclusion).

cit_fast: Simplified naturalization for ethnic Hungarians (knowledge of Hungarian + Hungarian origin) — without any requirement to reside in Hungary; for marriage to a Hungarian citizen from 5 years — a shortened period (about 3 years of joint residence in the marriage).
counts_note: There is no official digital nomad visa giving a path to permanent residence in Hungary under the general migration procedure (the White Card for remote workers is a separate short-term category, usually not counted towards the permanent residence/citizenship period).
presence: Continuous residence on a permanent residence permit is required before applying for citizenship.
language: Hungarian language (oral exam on the basics of the constitutional order in Hungarian).
children: Minor children are, as a rule, included in the parent's naturalisation application.

cit_fast: Vietnam's new citizenship law (2025 reform, in force in 2025) expanded the possibilities of retaining/acquiring citizenship for overseas Vietnamese and simplified a number of procedures, but for foreigners without Vietnamese roots the general permanent residence period for naturalisation remains about 5 years.
counts_note: There is no separate digital nomad visa in Vietnam (n_a); for ordinary work/business visas the detailed rules on counting toward naturalization residence were not found in open sources in sufficient detail.
presence: Permanent residence in Vietnam on the basis of a residence card (thẻ thường trú) for a set period is required.
language: Vietnamese language, knowledge of Vietnam's history/laws, absence of a threat to national security.
children: Minor children, as a rule, acquire citizenship together with the naturalizing parent under the general procedure.

cit_fast: 3 years in marriage to a Greek citizen and with a common child (or a longer marriage period without a child); for EU citizens/EU family members — different (shorter) periods. Law 4735/2020 established the requirement of 7 years of legal residence in the preceding 10 years for ordinary naturalisation.
counts_note: The Greek digital nomad visa (since 2021) gives a residence permit that formally counts as legal residence, but since the requirement is 7 of the previous 10 years, not continuous residence, the exact practice of crediting this particular category is not separately confirmed officially.
presence: 7 years of legal residence within the last 10 years before applying are required (not necessarily strictly continuous, but with substantial actual presence).
language: Test of knowledge of the Greek language (level B1) and Greek history/culture (PEGP exam).
children: Minor children living with the applicant parent in Greece, as a rule, acquire citizenship together with them on a derivative basis.

cit_fast: Simplified routes: no special term benefits for investors were identified in the Organic Law itself (general term — 5 years, since November 2023; previously 10), but an 'investor-resident' programme is mentioned in by-laws; for ethnic Georgians/persons with special merit — by decree of the President without a residence term or language requirement (art. 25 and art. 12 of the Organic Law).
counts_note: Georgia requires 5 years of continuous lawful residence for ordinary naturalisation (art. 12(1)(a) of the Organic Law as amended on 02.11.2023; previously 10); detailed official rules on counting the various types of residence permit (work, student, freelancer) are not sufficiently formalised in open sources in English.
presence: Continuous residence in Georgia for the established period before applying for citizenship is required.
language: Georgian language (oral and written exam), knowledge of the history and basics of law of Georgia.
children: Minor children, as a rule, acquire Georgian citizenship together with the naturalizing parent.

cit_fast: The accelerated period of 4 years of permanent residence is available to persons with a high level of integration (fluent Danish, stable employment), which according to the hint leads to a shorter total path to citizenship (about 6 years instead of 9 with exceptional integration/high-level language knowledge and no social benefits).
counts_note: Denmark has no separate digital nomad visa under general migration law; a residence permit for the self-employed (start-up/positive list) is usually full, but the exact counting rules are not confirmed in detail in open sources.
presence: Continuous residence in the territory of Denmark for the established period is required; a limited number of days of absence is allowed (usually no more than a few months over the whole period without interrupting the residence record).
language: Danish language (Prøve i Dansk 3 exam or higher) + a test on knowledge of Danish society, history and culture (Indfødsretsprøven).
children: Minor children are, as a rule, included in the parent's citizenship application (naturalisation through a special citizenship act adopted by Parliament twice a year — a feature of the Danish system, citizenship is granted by an act of parliament, not by an administrative decision).

cit_fast: For citizens of Spain and Latin American countries — 2 years of residence; for marriage to a Dominican — simplified procedure. For other foreigners — the ordinary naturalization procedure after legal residence.
counts_note: Migration Law No. 285-04 distinguishes residents (residencia) and non-residents; a residence permit for work/investment/pension counts as temporary residence (2 years), which converts to permanent residence, followed by the period toward naturalization. The digital nomad visa (since 2021) gives temporary stay, but its status for conversion to residency/citizenship is not unambiguously described in open sources — marked as unknown.
presence: Actual residence in the country during the period of residency is required; exact day thresholds are not detailed in open sources.
language: Spanish is mandatory; exam on the history/constitution of the Dominican Republic.
children: Minor children living with a resident parent are, as a rule, included in the parent's residence application; upon the parent's naturalisation, children may obtain citizenship in a simplified procedure when living together (details not guaranteed by an official source in English).

cit_fast: Citizenship by investment programme (Law 2018/2019, amendments published in March 2020): real estate from 300,000 USD in state projects (can be sold after 5 years), or a donation from 250,000 USD, or business investment 350,000+100 000 USD, or a bank deposit of 500,000 USD (refundable after 3 years). Vetting/approval takes from several months to a year; in 2025 Egypt reported granting 36 citizenships in a year amid stricter vetting.
counts_note: Permanent residence as a separate category is practically absent; ordinary naturalization requires long residence (about 10 years), the investment route is a separate accelerated path, unrelated to the residence period (counts=n_a for investment).
presence: Ordinary naturalisation requires long continuous residence in Egypt (by various estimates from 10 years); the investment route does not require physical residence.
language: For ordinary naturalization — knowledge of Arabic is presumed; for the investment route language/history tests are officially not required.
children: Minor children of the investor are usually included in the citizenship application together with the parent under the investment programme.

cit_fast: India has no formal permanent residence for most foreigners; for persons of Indian origin (OCI — Overseas Citizen of India) there is an almost lifelong visa, but it is not citizenship. Naturalisation under section 6 of the Citizenship Act 1955 requires residence in India for 12 of the last 14 years, including the last year continuously.
counts_note: India officially has no digital nomad visa (n_a); long-term visas (employment, student, X-visa for spouses) generally count towards the overall 12-year period provided continuous legal registration (FRRO).
presence: Physical presence in India for 12 months immediately before applying + a total of 11 of the previous 14 years is required.
language: Knowledge of one of the languages listed in the 8th Schedule to the Constitution of India is required (usually English is accepted informally for certain categories, but by law a regional/official language is needed).
children: Minor children of a naturalised parent may be included in the application and obtain citizenship together with the parent at the discretion of the authorities (section 6, Third Schedule).

cit_fast: Second Home Visa (launched 2023) gives up to 10 years of stay with a deposit from 2 billion IDR (~130,000 USD), but it is a temporary visa (ITAS/ITAP separately) and formally does not guarantee a path to citizenship; under the general 2006 citizenship law naturalisation requires 5 years of continuous residence on permanent residence (KITAP) or 10 years with breaks.
counts_note: Indonesia's remote/digital nomad visa (E33G, for remote work for a foreign employer) does not give the right to permanent residence and does not count towards the period for naturalisation — noted explicitly (no); the Second Home Visa by itself is not a path to residence/citizenship, it is a separate long-term stay visa.
presence: Obtaining a KITAP (permanent residence) and then citizenship requires continuous lawful residence; dual citizenship for adults is not permitted — only for children under 18/21 (dwi kewarganegaraan terbatas).
language: Knowledge of the Indonesian language (Bahasa Indonesia) and recognition of Pancasila/the state ideology are required for naturalization.
children: Children of foreigners born in a mixed marriage may hold limited dual citizenship until age 18–21, then must choose one; for children whose parents are both foreigners there is no separate simplified route.

cit_fast: For spouses of Irish citizens — 3 years of legal residence (out of the last 4 years) instead of 5; a separate simplified route for refugees/stateless persons (3 years). Ireland has no formal separate permanent residence status distinct from the naturalisation conditions — Stamp 4 (long-term residence permit) can usually be obtained after ~5 years of legal work/residence.
counts_note: Naturalization requires 5 years of 'reckonable residence' out of the last 9 years, including a continuous final year; time on a student visa counts only at half (Stamp 2). Ireland has no separate digital nomad visa (n_a).
presence: 5 years of 'reckonable residence' out of the last 9 years, the last year continuous before the application.
language: There is no formal language exam or test of history/constitution for naturalisation in Ireland.
children: Minor children of a parent who becomes an Irish citizen do not receive citizenship automatically — a separate naturalization application is filed for the child (residence requirements for children are softer / at the minister's discretion).

cit_fast: Marriage to an Italian citizen — 2 years of residence in Italy (or 3 years abroad), halved if there are children; for persons of Italian descent — simplified procedure under 'ius sanguinis' with no residence requirement.
counts_note: Ordinary naturalisation requires 10 years of legal continuous residence (for non-EU citizens); EU long-term resident status (Permesso di soggiorno UE per soggiornanti di lungo periodo) is available after 5 years. The digital nomad visa (introduced in 2024) is too new — its effect on the residence period for citizenship has not been officially clarified (unknown).
presence: 10 years of continuous lawful residence in Italy for ordinary naturalization; short trips are allowed, but proof of continuous registration at the place of residence (residenza anagrafica) is required.
language: An Italian language exam at level B1 or higher is mandatory (CILS/CELI/PLIDA certificate or equivalent), a history/constitution test is formally not required, but an interview at the prefecture is possible.
children: Minor children living with the parent at the time of the oath/naturalisation decree automatically acquire Italian citizenship together with the parent.

cit_fast: A simplified procedure is provided for certain categories (ethnic Kazakh oralmans, spouses of Kazakhstan citizens — usually a shortened period); for other foreigners — the general procedure after 5 years of permanent residence on a residence permit.
counts_note: The Law "On Citizenship of the Republic of Kazakhstan" links naturalization to permanent residence (residence permit/'permanent resident') issued by the Ministry of Interior; separate categories by visa types (investor/passive income/nomad) are not detailed in open official sources (unknown).
presence: Continuous permanent residence in Kazakhstan for 5 years on a residence permit before filing is required.
language: Knowledge of the state (Kazakh) language sufficient for communication is required (testing at the commission's discretion); also knowledge of the basics of legislation.
children: Minor children, as a rule, acquire Kazakh citizenship together with the naturalising parent when residing together and with the consent of the other parent (if applicable).

cit_fast: In Canada there are no fast-track routes to citizenship bypassing Permanent Resident (PR) status — all citizenship applicants must first hold PR status, then accumulate physical presence.
counts_note: For citizenship only time after obtaining Permanent Resident status counts, 1095 days (3 years) of physical presence in the last 5 years are needed; before obtaining PR, time on temporary status (work/study by permit) counts at half, maximum 365 days of credit. Canada officially does not issue a digital nomad visa (n_a).
presence: 1,095 days (3 years) of physical presence in Canada within the last 5 years immediately before applying, plus the requirement to file tax returns for 3 of 5 years.
language: Knowledge of English or French is required (level CLB 4) for applicants aged 18–54, plus a test on knowledge of Canada (history, values, institutions, geography) in English/French.
children: Minor children with permanent residence living with the applicant parent apply for citizenship simultaneously with the parent (simplified procedure for children under 18, the Canada knowledge test is not required for children under 18).

cit_fast: Qualified/high-paid workers — 3–4 years (depending on the level of Greek) under the 2023–2024 amendments; marriage to a Cypriot man/woman — as a rule 3 years of marriage + 2 years of residence. The citizenship by investment programme (Cyprus Investment Programme) was closed in November 2020 and is not in operation.
counts_note: Ordinary path under the 2023/2024 amendments: 7 full years (2555 days) of legal residence out of the last 10 years + additionally the last 12 months of continuous residence before applying (so effectively 8 years in total), plus a Greek B1 certificate. The digital nomad visa (limited by quota) gives a temporary residence permit, but no official clarification on full credit toward this period was found — kept as half/uncertain.
presence: 7 of the last 10 years of legal residence + the last year (12 months) continuously before applying = effectively 8 years; for highly qualified workers — 3–4 years.
language: Greek language at level B1 (certificate from a written exam, or a school certificate or university diploma with instruction in Greek) and an exam on knowledge of the political and social reality of Cyprus (held in Greek; in 2026 the session is 04.07.2026, applications 19.05–02.06.2026, fee 20 euros). For highly qualified workers: A2 with 4 years of residence or B1 with 3 years.
children: Minor children of a naturalizing parent are, as a rule, included in the application and receive citizenship together with them if they live together in Cyprus.

cit_fast: Officially the law does not single out separate fast-track routes for ordinary foreigners (except persons of Chinese origin reuniting their family in the PRC, or persons married to a Chinese citizen and residing in the country); in practice naturalisation of foreigners is extremely rare regardless of category.
counts_note: The 1980 Nationality Law of the PRC formally allows naturalization on the basis of close kinship with a PRC citizen, permanent residence in China or 'other legitimate reasons', but does not specify a minimum residence permit period by visa type; in practice decisions are made individually and extremely rarely for persons without Chinese roots/marriage. China does not issue digital nomad or passive income visas (n_a).
presence: The law requires residence in China, but the specific number of years for ordinary (not kinship-based) naturalization is not officially set; in practice, many years (usually 5+) of continuous residence on a Green Card/residence permit are expected.
language: No official standardised language/history exams for naturalisation are published; knowledge of Chinese is presumed in practice for integration and the interview.
children: Official detailed rules on the automatic inclusion of minor children in a parent's application were not found in open sources; individual consideration is presumed.

cit_fast: For citizens of Spain and Latin American countries under a treaty — 1 year of legal residence; for marriage to a Colombian or having a Colombian child — 2 years of residence. For other foreigners — 5 years of continuous residence.
counts_note: The resident visa (visa 'R' — temporary resident migration visa) after 5 years gives the right to naturalisation as a general rule; permanent residence status as a separate category is effectively not distinguished in Colombia — the long-term Visa R performs a similar function. The effect of the digital nomad visa (Visa V — Nomad, introduced in 2022) on the residence period for naturalisation has not been officially clarified (unknown).
presence: 5 years of continuous legal residence in Colombia for the ordinary naturalization procedure (Ley 43 de 1993, as amended).
language: Knowledge of Spanish is required (oral exam/interview when applying to the Cancillería).
children: Minor children of a foreigner who legally reside in Colombia can, as a rule, obtain citizenship by the fact of permanent residence separately from the parent's naturalization, or together with it upon application — the procedure is regulated by the Cancillería individually.

cit_fast: Marriage to a citizen of Costa Rica (after 2 years of marriage and residence) and having children born in Costa Rica give the right to naturalisation with a reduced period (obtaining residencia como pariente/casado); citizens of Spain and other Central American countries — 5 years instead of 7 (Ley 1155).
counts_note: Under Ley 1155 (Naturalización por Residencia), resident status (DIMEX) is required for a minimum of 7 years for most foreigners (5 years for Spanish-speaking/Latin American citizens). Ley 1902 provides an alternative path after 20 years of continuous residence in the country (even without formal resident status) - rarely used. The Costa Rica digital nomad visa (2021 law) grants temporary stay, but officially does not lead to permanent residence/residency for naturalization (unknown).
presence: 7 years of residence as a legal resident (usually after temporary status, then permanent resident) for most foreigners under Ley 1155; residence must be documented (no long absences).
language: Knowledge of Spanish (exam) and of the history/constitution/symbols of Costa Rica (exam at the TSE) is required.
children: Minor children of a foreigner legally residing with them in Costa Rica, as a rule, receive resident status together with the parent and can apply for citizenship upon reaching the relevant period of residence or simultaneously with the parent's naturalisation, subject to individual review.

cit_fast: The law allows a reduction of the general 5-year period (up to no residence requirement) for persons with special merits (outstanding achievements in science, technology, culture, sport), as well as a simplified procedure for ethnic Kyrgyz and citizens of CIS states under separate agreements.
counts_note: The law 'On Citizenship of the Kyrgyz Republic' links naturalization to 5 years of continuous residence on a residence permit; details by visa type (investor/nomad/passive income) are absent from open sources (unknown).
presence: Continuous residence in Kyrgyzstan for 5 years on a residence permit before applying (for most applicants); for special merits the term may be shortened.
language: Knowledge of the state (Kyrgyz) or official (Russian) language sufficient for communication is required.
children: Minor children generally acquire Kyrgyz citizenship together with the naturalizing parent when living together.

cit_fast: The separate status of 'non-citizen' (nepilsonis) applies only to a specific historical category of permanent residents of Latvia from the Soviet period, access for new applicants is closed.
counts_note: The usual period for naturalisation is 10 years of legal permanent residence (5 years to obtain permanent residence + another 5 years of waiting before applying for citizenship). The passive_income status is not clarified in open sources (n_a deliberately not set - left as a separate field below).
presence: For ordinary naturalization — 10 years of permanent residence in Latvia
language: A Latvian language exam is mandatory (standard level for naturalization), as well as a test on the history of Latvia, the text of the anthem and the basics of the constitution.
children: Minor children living with the naturalizing parent are, as a rule, included in the application and obtain citizenship together with them, provided the general conditions of legal residence are met.

cit_fast: Lithuanian origin (persons of Lithuanian nationality and their descendants) — a simplified procedure for restoring/acquiring citizenship without a residence period requirement; marriage to a Lithuanian citizen (from 7 years of marriage) may shorten the overall residence period.
counts_note: The Lithuanian Citizenship Law requires 10 years of continuous residence for ordinary naturalization (5 years to obtain permanent residence, then a further period up to 10 years in total). In 2024 a constitutional referendum on expanding dual citizenship was held — the turnout threshold was not reached, the referendum was declared not valid, and the existing restrictions on dual citizenship for non-Lithuanians by origin remain.
presence: 10 years of continuous legal residence in Lithuania for the ordinary naturalization procedure (including the permanent residence period).
language: An exam in the Lithuanian language and an exam on the basics of the Constitution of the Republic of Lithuania are mandatory.
children: Minor children of a naturalizing parent living with them in Lithuania, as a rule, acquire citizenship together with the parent under a joint application.

cit_fast: For spouses of Luxembourg citizens the required period of lawful residence is shortened (as a rule to 3 years of living together in marriage); there is no separate investor fast track to citizenship.
counts_note: The Luxembourg citizenship law (as amended in 2017) requires 5 years of legal residence immediately before the application; study period counts only partially. Luxembourg does not issue a separate digital nomad visa (n_a) — for remote work for a foreign employer a general EU/employment or self-employment residence permit is usually used.
presence: 5 years of legal residence in Luxembourg immediately before applying, including the last year continuously.
language: An oral exam in Luxembourgish is mandatory (level B1 oral / A2 written) along with the course 'Vivre ensemble au Luxembourg' (living together in Luxembourg society, 24 hours).
children: Minor children of the naturalising parent living with them generally acquire Luxembourg citizenship together with the parent automatically upon joint application.

cit_fast: Marriage to a Malaysian citizen — a shortened term (usually from 2 years of residence in the marriage under Article 15(1) of the Constitution), the decision remains in any case at the government's discretion.
counts_note: Naturalization under Article 19 of the Constitution of Malaysia requires residence in the country for at least 10 of the last 12 years (including 12 months immediately before applying), the decision is entirely at the government's discretion and is not guaranteed even with formal compliance. The MM2H programme (My Second Home, for passive income/retirees) does not directly lead to permanent residence or citizenship - participants remain on a long-term social visa outside the labour market (passive_income=no); digital nomad visas (DE Rantau) are also not recognized as grounds for residency/citizenship (no).
presence: 10 of the last 12 years of residence in Malaysia, including the 12 months immediately before applying; naturalisation is not guaranteed even with formal compliance with the terms.
language: Knowledge of Malay (Bahasa Malaysia) is required at a level sufficient for an interview.
children: No official data on the automatic inclusion of a foreigner's minor children in the parent's naturalization application was found in open sources; the children's status is considered individually.

cit_fast: The citizenship-by-investment programme (MEIN/Malta Citizenship by Merit) was found incompatible with EU law by the judgment of the CJEU (case C-181/23) of 29 April 2025; Malta stopped accepting new applications under this programme in 2026. Passports previously issued under this programme remain valid. Discretionary naturalization 'for special merits' formally remains outside the closed investment programme, but the details are unclear.
counts_note: Formally, Maltese law sets 5 years of residence for naturalisation, but in practice (per unofficial data and the practice of law firms) ordinary applicants wait for a decision substantially longer — in fact up to ~15 years because of discretionary and slow administration. The citizenship-by-investment programme is closed (investment=no) after the EU Court decision of 29.04.2025.
presence: Formally 5 years of residence in Malta (12 months continuous before filing + 4 years out of the previous 6), but the actual practice of granting citizenship via this route is extremely slow and not guaranteed.
language: Official detailed language requirements for standard naturalization are not specified in open sources; a base level of integration is expected.
children: Minor children of a naturalizing parent can, as a rule, be included in the naturalization process if living together in Malta (details of the ordinary procedure are covered to a limited extent in open sources).

cit_fast: Through the birth of a child who is a citizen of Mexico (hijos mexicanos) the period is reduced to 2 years of residence; marriage to a Mexican citizen is also an accelerated route; for citizens of Latin American countries and the Iberian Peninsula (Spain/Portugal) — simplified conditions. The Spanish language exam is not required for persons over 60, refugees and minors.
counts_note: Mexico counts the period of legal residence (temporal/permanente) regardless of visa type under the general rule of art. 20 of the Nationality Law; no separate restrictions on the visa de nómada digital (temporal por medios propios/remote worker) found in official SRE materials — marked as unknown, needs clarification with INM.
presence: 5 years of continuous legal residence (temporal or permanente) with a resident card; if a Mexican child is born — 2 years
language: An exam on knowledge of Spanish and basic information about Mexico (history/culture); refugees, minors and persons 60+ are exempt
children: Minor children legally residing with the applicant parent may obtain citizenship together with the parent under a simplified procedure (hijos sujetos a patria potestad)

cit_fast: 3 years when married to a Moldovan citizen; 3 years when living together with parents/children who are Moldovan citizens; 5 years for persons who lived in the country before the age of 18; 8 years for stateless persons/persons with international protection. The previously existing CBI programme (citizenship by investment) was abolished in 2020.
counts_note: The official source (ASP) describes only the total period of legal residence without a breakdown by visa type; no separate "digital nomad" visa for freelancers/remote work was identified in Moldova — legalisation is usually via a residence permit based on employment/entrepreneurship or family reunification
presence: 10 years of continuous legal residence (total period) on a residence permit
language: Knowledge of the Romanian (state) language and the basics of the Constitution of Moldova
children: The official ASP page does not detail the procedure for the applicant's minor children separately from the general rule "3 years when living together with children who are Moldovan citizens"; for children who are not citizens the general procedure of joint naturalisation probably applies — needs clarification

cit_fast: 3 years in case of marriage/registered partnership with a citizen of the Netherlands and living together. As of September 2026 the standard term remains 5 years of continuous legal residence; in 2024–2025 the cabinet proposed increasing the term to 10 years, but according to available data the law was not finally adopted and did not enter into force by the stated date — additional verification of the bill's status as of the reference date (September 2026) is required.
counts_note: A digital nomad visa as a separate category officially does not exist in the Netherlands (freelance/DAFT only for Americans under the 1956 treaty); a student residence permit is usually counted at half under the general EMN practice for EU countries
presence: 5 years of continuous legal residence (main residence permit option); no long absences
language: Integration exam (inburgeringsexamen) at a level of at least A2/B1, includes knowledge of Dutch society
children: Minor children can be included in the parent's naturalization application (mede-naturalisatie) if living together

cit_fast: There are no separate fast-track routes for investors — the general physical presence period of 5 years (1,350 days) on Resident Visa status (not a temporary visa) applies to all categories equally.
counts_note: Only time on a Resident Visa (permanent residence) counts; time on temporary (work/student) visas does not count at all towards the 5 years required for citizenship — important: the 'work visa → PR' stage does not count towards the naturalisation period, counting starts only after obtaining the Resident Visa. There is no digital nomad visa in New Zealand (n_a)
presence: At least 1,350 days of physical presence in New Zealand within the 5 years immediately before filing, on Resident Visa status, including at least 240 days in each of the last 5 years
language: Spoken English (interview), knowledge of the rights and duties of a New Zealand citizen
children: Minor children (under 16) are included in the parent's application automatically when residence conditions are met; for children 16+ a separate application is required

cit_fast: The period can be reduced to 6 years with a confirmed annual income not below the established minimum (366,675 NOK per 2024 data / 384,348 NOK per 2025 data — the amount is indexed annually, the exact figure for 2026 is to be clarified at the time of filing). Reduced periods also apply to spouses of Norwegian citizens.
counts_note: UDI counts permitted legal residence as a whole; student residence permits are traditionally counted at half under general European practice (requires final confirmation from UDI); Norway has no separate visa for remote freelancers — a classic work visa/skilled worker residence permit will probably be needed
presence: 7 years of residence in the last 10 years (general rule) on a permit that gives the right to permanent residence, plus a continuity requirement; with income above the threshold — a shortened period of 6 years of continuous residence
language: Norwegian or Sami language — oral/written exam (usually level A2 oral / A1 written, requirements depend on age) plus a test on knowledge of Norwegian society (samfunnskunnskap)
children: Minor children can be included in the parent's application (medsøker) if they live together in Norway

cit_fast: Since 2021 a decree has been in force allowing the granting of UAE citizenship (by invitation of the authorities, not by application) to investors, specialists, scientists, doctors, cultural figures and other categories at the government's discretion — this is not an open programme for everyone, but a selective decision of the Emirati authorities; there is no mass route for an ordinary migrant/freelancer.
counts_note: There is effectively no classic naturalisation 'by length of residence' for ordinary residents in the UAE — the standard route under the 1972 Citizenship Law requires 30 years of residence (20 years for Arabs) and approval at the discretion of the authorities, which makes the 'visa types' counter of little use; the selective 2021 programme is by invitation, not by application
presence: 30 years of continuous legal residence (standard path) or a selective invitation from the authorities regardless of length of residence (2021 programme)
language: Arabic is mandatory for standard naturalization
children: When citizenship is obtained under the selective programme, minor children may be included at the authorities' discretion; there is no separate public regulation

cit_fast: There is no separate fast-track route through investment for the final term — a CBI programme as such does not exist in Paraguay; in fact it is one of the fastest 'ordinary' paths to citizenship in the world (temporary residence permit → permanent residence after ~2 years → citizenship after another 3 years of permanent residence, about 5 years in total including the temporary residence permit)
counts_note: Paraguay grants a residence permit on the criterion of financial self-sufficiency/income (including passive and from remote work) practically without restrictions — counted as ordinary residence for naturalization purposes
presence: Physical presence is required to a minimal degree (no strict rule on the number of days per year), but the applicant must demonstrate ties to the country and not leave for long continuous periods
language: Spoken Spanish (basic exam/interview)
children: Minor children receive citizenship together with the naturalizing parent if they live together

cit_fast: 3 years of permanent residence (karta stałego pobytu) + marriage to a Polish citizen of 3 years or more — an alternative path; also naturalization is possible by decision of the President of Poland regardless of the length of residence (discretionary path, not guaranteed). Legislative initiatives to tighten the requirements are being discussed (2025–2026), but the current term as of the reference date is approximately 3 years after obtaining permanent residence (in total ~8 years from the start of legal residence).
counts_note: Poland counts time on a karta pobytu (temporary residence permit) towards the total period for permanent residence (usually 5 years of continuous legal residence); student time is traditionally counted at a reduced rate under common European practice; for 'digital nomads' there is formally no separate visa category in Poland
presence: 5 years of continuous legal residence for permanent residence, then at least 3 years of residence with permanent residence and knowledge of Polish (B1) for naturalization on application
language: Polish language at least level B1 (certificate); when obtained by decision of the president, the language is not always required
children: Minor children can obtain citizenship together with the naturalizing parent if they live together and the other parent consents (if applicable)

cit_fast: For citizens of the EU and CPLP (Community of Portuguese Language Countries) — 7 years instead of 10. REFORM: the final law is Lei Orgânica n.º 1/2026, de 18 de maio (after the Constitutional Court's review of an earlier version of the law, signed by the president in 2025 and challenged in the CC — see Acórdão 1133/2025). The law was published on 18.05.2026 and entered into force on 19.05.2026, increasing the standard naturalisation period from 5 to 10 years (7 years for EU/CPLP). TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS CONFIRMED: applications filed BEFORE 19.05.2026 (processos pendentes) are governed by the previous version of the law (old periods — 5 years / 7 years EU-CPLP); the new rules (10/7 years) apply only to applications filed AFTER 19.05.2026 — that is, the date of filing the citizenship application determines the applicable period, not the date the residence permit was issued.
counts_note: Before the 2026 reform, time on any type of legal residence permit (including D7 passive income, D8 digital nomad, Golden Visa) counted towards the citizenship period as ordinary 'residência legal'. The official implementing acts for the new law are to be adopted within 90 days after 19.05.2026 — check before applying whether the same principle of counting residence permit types is retained.
presence: Until 19.05.2026: 5 years (7 for EU/CPLP). From 19.05.2026 (for applications filed after this date): 10 years (7 for EU/CPLP). The former law applies to applications already filed.
language: Portuguese language at A2 level (CIPLE exam or equivalent)
children: Minor children born or residing in Portugal for a certain time with a resident parent may apply for citizenship on separate grounds (birth in the country + conditions of the parents' residence), or receive a residence permit together with the parent and naturalise later on general grounds

cit_fast: Reduced periods (4 years) for spouses of Romanian citizens and for persons adopted by a Romanian citizen, and also for certain investments/significant contributions to the Romanian economy by decision of a commission; for ethnic Romanians and citizens of Moldova simplified grounds also apply (not relevant to the sample household).
counts_note: The total period of 8 years is the cumulative period of legal residence on the territory of Romania (not necessarily only on permanent residence); student time under general EU practice is counted at half; for freelancers/remote workers there is de facto no separate 'digital nomad' visa category — legalization usually goes through a residence permit for freelance specialists (freelancer visa) with a status similar to a work one
presence: 8 years of continuous legal residence in Romania (for those not connected to Romania by origin) for standard naturalization on application
language: Romanian language — a basic oral exam, knowledge of the Constitution and state symbols of Romania
children: Minor children are included in the parent's naturalization application (dobândesc cetăţenia română împreună cu părintele) if they live together

cit_fast: No official fast-track routes for ordinary immigrants identified; citizenship is granted by decision of the Council of Ministers of the TRNC (discretionary), the formal minimum residence period on a resident visa is about 7 years, but approval is not guaranteed even if the formal conditions are met.
counts_note: IMPORTANT: the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC) is a partially recognised state, recognised only by Turkey; most countries of the world, do not recognise its citizenship as separate from the Republic of Cyprus. Reliable official information on the counting of different residence permit types towards the citizenship period could not be found — a separate consultation with the local immigration department is required
presence: Approximately 5 to 7 years of continuous residence on a resident visa (requires confirmation from the official immigration department of the TRNC)
language: Turkish language (oral exam) is mandatory
children: No official data found on the procedure for the applicant's minor children — needs clarification

cit_fast: Officially, under art. 14 of the Law on Citizenship of the Republic of Serbia the standard naturalisation procedure requires NOT 7-8, but only 3 YEARS of continuous permanent residence (stalno nastanjenje/prebivalište) before applying - the draft contained an error. 3 years of marriage to a Serbian citizen with cohabitation is an accelerated route on the same conditions (in fact the same 3-year 'stalno nastanjenje' period); a temporary residence permit (privremeni boravak) is obtained relatively quickly (within a few months on the basis of work, business, real estate or independent income), after which a transition to permanent residence status (stalno nastanjenje) is required, from which the 3-year period is counted.
counts_note: The Serbian citizenship law (Zakon o državljanstvu Republike Srbije) generally requires 3 years of permanent residence (stalno nastanjenje) immediately before the application + a significant total period of legal residence in the country; the exact rules for crediting different types of residence permits (work, self-employment/freelance through registration as a 'preduzetnik', property ownership) are set out in open sources without a single summary table — marked as unknown to be clarified with MUP Srbije
presence: 3 years of permanent residence (stalno nastanjenje/permanent residence) immediately before applying for citizenship, with a total legal stay in the country usually of 5 years or more
language: Knowledge of the Serbian language (basic conversational level, confirmed at an interview), knowledge of the basics of the Constitution
children: Minor children are included in the parent's naturalization application if they live together and the other parent consents (if applicable)

cit_fast: The formal minimum is 2 years of PR (Permanent Resident) and age 21+ to apply, but in practice, according to immigration consultants, applications from persons with PR for less than 3–6 years are rarely approved; for students who have lived in Singapore for 3+ years and at least 1 year with PR, a separate category applies.
counts_note: There is no digital nomad visa in Singapore (n_a); to obtain permanent residence the work visa (Employment Pass) is the standard route; time on PR status counts, not time on a work visa before obtaining PR
presence: Formally from 2 years of permanent residence before filing the application (per the official ICA page); actual approval practice — usually 3–6 years of permanent residence
language: There is no official language exam for adult citizenship applicants as a general rule (unlike permanent residence), but English/national languages are important for integration; proof of settled residence, work/income, and absence of criminal records is required
children: Minor children (under 21, unmarried) can be included in the application of the parent-applicant for citizenship

cit_fast: 8 years of continuous permanent residence (trvalý pobyt) with a level of Slovak language of at least A2, or alternatively 10 years of residence in the country in total without the obligatory permanent residence status throughout; for spouses of Slovak citizens and on some other grounds (significant contribution in the interests of Slovakia) — separate reduced conditions by decision of the ministry.
counts_note: Slovakia counts residence time under various types of residence permit as a general rule; for freelancers/remote workers there is no separate visa category, legalisation is usually through a residence permit based on business (živnosť) or employment, which under general practice is counted in full; student time is traditionally counted at a reduced rate
presence: 8 years of continuous permanent residence (trvalý pobyt) with A2 language, or 10 years of legal residence in total (less strict variant, details for this variant require clarification with the Ministerstvo vnútra)
language: Slovak language at A2 level (oral and written test) for the 8-year permanent residence path
children: Minor children can be included in the parent's naturalization application if they live together

cit_fast: Accelerated routes (3 years) — for spouses of Slovenian citizens after a marriage of a certain length and joint residence; for persons born in the former Yugoslavia there are separate simplified grounds
counts_note: The total term of 10 years is the cumulative legal residence in the country, of which the last 5 years must be continuous immediately before the application; the specific crediting of student and 'digital nomad' residence towards the total term needs clarification with the relevant Slovenian Ministry of Interior
presence: 10 years of legal residence overall, of which the last 5 years continuous before the application
language: Slovenian language (exam, usually at level no lower than A2/B1) and basic knowledge of the state structure of Slovenia
children: Minor children are included in the parent's naturalisation application if living together

cit_fast: 3 years instead of 5 for those married to a US citizen and living together; minor children of green card holders often obtain citizenship automatically under the Child Citizenship Act 2000 under certain conditions (residence in the USA with a citizen parent, age under 18), without a separate N-400 filing
counts_note: For naturalisation only time with Green Card (Lawful Permanent Resident) status counts — temporary work/student visas (H-1B, F-1) by themselves do not give the right to naturalisation and are not counted until a green card is obtained; a digital nomad visa does not exist in the USA (n_a)
presence: 5 years of continuous residence with a Green Card + physical presence of at least 30 months out of those 5 years + at least 3 months of residence in the state/district of filing
language: English (speaking, reading, writing) and a test on US history and government (civics); exemptions by age/length of residence (e.g. the 50/20 and 55/15 rules)
children: Minor children of green card holders residing in the US with the parent, as a rule, automatically become citizens upon the parent's naturalization (Child Citizenship Act), without taking separate exams

cit_fast: No separate fast-track investment programmes identified
counts_note: Official detailed information on counting specific types of residence permits towards the naturalization period was not found in English on the website of the Tajik Ministry of Foreign Affairs; a direct inquiry to the consulate/OVIR of Tajikistan is needed to clarify the practice
presence: 5 years of continuous residence on the basis of a residence permit (under the general norm of the Law on Citizenship of the Republic of Tajikistan)
language: Knowledge of the state (Tajik) language at a basic level (per the general norm of citizenship legislation, the exact exam criteria are not detailed in open sources)
children: No official detailed data on the procedure for the applicant's minor children was found; by the general practice of post-Soviet countries children usually receive citizenship together with the parent when living together — needs confirmation

cit_fast: There is no separate fast-track for ordinary foreigners; the naturalisation quota is limited (about 100 people per year per country of origin according to unofficial data from consultants), the decision is made by the Ministry of Interior after an interview and vetting; marriage to a citizen of Thailand shortens the required residence period.
counts_note: Thai permanent residence is obtained by holders of non-immigrant visas (Non-Immigrant B — work, investment, marriage etc.) after 3 years of continuous residence; the digital nomad visa (Destination Thailand Visa, DTV, introduced in 2024) does NOT lead to permanent residence/citizenship — explicitly noted as unsuitable for counting towards the naturalisation period
presence: 3 years on a non-immigrant visa → application for permanent residence (within the annual quota) → 5 years with permanent residence to apply for citizenship; practically 8+ years in total
language: Thai language (oral and written test) and singing the Thai anthem at the interview
children: Minor children can receive a residence permit/status together with a parent, but a separate automatic path to citizenship together with a naturalizing parent is not described in detail in open sources — needs clarification

cit_fast: Citizenship by real estate investment programme — legal basis: art. 12(b) of Law No. 5901 + Presidential Decree No. 5042 (sets the thresholds). Minimum threshold CONFIRMED: 400,000 USD (unchanged since June 2022), the property must be held for at least 3 years. Processing time per Kulaçoğlu — from 4 months to 1 year («ortalama 4 ay ila 1 yıl»); with a deadline of the older child turning 18, apply with a margin
counts_note: The key question for the sample profile: years on a tourist ikamet (kısa dönem ikamet izni, not tied to work/marriage/real estate) are NOT counted towards the 5-year naturalisation period under the ordinary article 11 of Law No. 5901. According to the practice of Turkish immigration lawyers (e.g. Kulaçoğlu Hukuk Bürosu, Keleş Hukuk), the general naturalisation procedure requires a residence permit that demonstrates 'niyet-i ikamet' (intention to settle) — this is a long-term residence permit (uzun dönem ikamet izni), a residence permit on the basis of marriage/family (aile ikamet izni), a work or student visa, or a real-estate residence permit; a purely tourist short-term ikamet not tied to work, real estate or marriage is not legally recognised as sufficient to demonstrate an intention to settle in the country and in practice is NOT counted by the Göç İdaresi Başkanlığı (migration service) towards the general 5-year period for naturalisation. The non-counting of a tourist residence permit is confirmed by a direct provision of the Regulation on the Implementation of the Citizenship Law (art. 16/2-c, see below) and by an official NVI document, as well as by explanations of law firms. Continuity (kesintisizlik): during the entire 5-year period the total absence from the country must not exceed 12 months ('consecutive' vs 'per year' is not specified separately — the total sum of days/months of absence over the whole period is counted, not by years). A switch from one type of residence permit to another (e.g. from a tourist one to a real-estate one) does not in itself 'reset' the years physically lived in Turkey, but since the tourist years were not counted initially, the real count of the 'full' 5-year period starts anew from the moment of receiving the real-estate residence permit (year 2026). For the citizenship-by-investment programme ($400,000) the past migration status does not matter at all — this route follows a separate, accelerated procedure (Cumhurbaşkanlığı kararı, art. 11 of the Citizenship Law, item 'İstisnai vatandaşlık'), independent of the length of residence. CONFIRMED FROM THE PRIMARY SOURCE (text of Law No. 5901 from mevzuat.gov.tr): art. 11(b) requires “kesintisiz beş yıl ikamet” (five years of continuous residence), the law itself does not list the types of residence permit, but the non-counting of a tourist residence permit is a direct provision of the Regulation on the Implementation of the Citizenship Law (Yönetmelik 2010/139, art. 16/2-c: residence for the purpose of “öğrenim, turistik … amaçlarla” does not show an intention to settle) and of the official NVI document (“turistik amaçlı ikamet tezkeresiyle … ikamet edilmesi … geçerli ikamet olarak kabul edilmez”). Article 12 (istisnai vatandaşlık, exceptional naturalisation) in its main list (industrial investments, outstanding merits) does NOT mention real estate directly in the text of the basic law — the route through purchasing real estate for 400,000 USD was added by a sub-statutory act (Presidential decree No. 5042 to art. 12(b)), it is a separate ground, independent of the 5-year residence period.
presence: Ordinary naturalization: 5 years of continuous residence, absence totalling no more than 12 months over the whole period; investment programme: a permanent residence requirement is effectively absent, it is important to keep ownership of the property for at least 3 years
language: Ordinary naturalization: Turkish at a basic conversational level (oral interview); investment programme — language not required
children: Minor children living with the applicant parent (including those with a separate residence permit of the same type) are included in the application and receive citizenship together with the parent automatically, under both programmes (ordinary and investment) For the investment programme the age of a "minor" is counted: per the decision of the Ankara Court of Appeal (09.12.2024) - at the date of application; per the practice of the migration service described by lawyers in 2026 - possibly at the date of the decision (details - review_note). A child naturalizes independently after turning 18.

counts_note: Citizenship is acquired via permanent residence (for this one must live in the country lawfully; the specific type of activity does not matter separately), an important requirement is prior renunciation of existing citizenship
presence: permanent residence for the established period before applying
language: knowledge of the state (Uzbek) language at a basic level
children: minor children usually acquire citizenship together with the parent when a joint application is filed

counts_note: 3 years of legal residence are required if there is an 'established family' in Uruguay (marriage/recognised cohabitation or children from a relationship in the country); without family — 5 years. For a single parent with children, if there is no Uruguayan spouse, the 5-year term as for a person without family in the country most likely applies, unless another basis is officially recognised
presence: residence must be 'habitual' (permanent); continuous absences of more than 6 months in a row interrupt the counting of the period
language: understanding and command of Spanish (oral, no formal level exam)
children: the official source does not specify a separate procedure for minors; in practice children receive citizenship together with the parent/by the parent's residence

counts_note: Commonwealth Act No. 473 requires 10 years of continuous residence (reduced to 5 years under a number of conditions: marriage to a Filipino citizen, birth in the Philippines, teaching, holding a patent for a useful invention, etc.)
presence: continuous residence throughout the whole period before applying, with restrictions on long absences
language: command of English or Tagalog (Filipino) or a local dialect
children: the law does not explicitly provide for the automatic extension of a parent's naturalization to foreign minor children; the children's status is usually determined separately (length of residence etc. are taken into account)

counts_note: Since 1 October 2024 the total residence period for citizenship has been increased from 5 to 8 years; the shortened period of 5 years - with confirmed knowledge of Finnish/Swedish or for the spouse of a Finnish citizen/stateless persons. Since 17.12.2025 for persons with international protection the period is also 8 years, counted from the first continuous residence permit CONFIRMED: the reform tightening the conditions for the permanent residence permit (pysyvä oleskelulupa) came into force on 8 January 2026 (Finnish Government/Migri): the period for permanent residence was increased to 6 years, plus requirements for language and 2 years of work experience. The period for citizenship (a track separate from permanent residence) remains 8 years under the general rule since 1.10.2024, 5 years with confirmed B1+ Finnish/Swedish.
presence: permanent (habitual) residence in Finland during the calculation period is required, with limits on the number of days of absence
language: confirmed knowledge of Finnish or Swedish (YKI certificate or equivalent); at level B1+ the term is reduced to 5 years
children: children aged 15-17 can be included as co-applicants in the parent's application (the same eased 5-year period is required with the language condition); younger children are listed in the parent's application on an additional form

cit_fast: 2 years upon graduating from a French university (a diploma of at least master level) instead of the standard 5 years
counts_note: Naturalisation by decree (naturalisation par décret) requires 5 years of residence in France ('stage'); the application can be submitted once this period is reached, a separate 'permanent residence first' is not required as a mandatory stage, although in practice a residence card (carte de séjour) is often obtained, then a residence permit
presence: residence in France ('résidence habituelle') throughout the entire qualifying period, actual residence is assessed (housing, work/income, integration)
language: French at least B2 (oral and written, CECRL scale) for applications under the decree (naturalization, reintegration) submitted from 01.01.2026 (previously B1); from the same date — a civic exam: 40 questions in French, pass mark 32 out of 40 (80 %), 45 minutes.
children: minor unmarried children living with the naturalising parent automatically acquire French citizenship if named in the parent's naturalisation decree

counts_note: Naturalization 'on the basis of residence' requires continuous legal residence (usually counted cumulatively: several years of temporary residence permit + permanent residence permit), in total about 8 years under the general rule (5 years for permanent residence + at least another period on permanent residence/length of residence)
presence: a valid temporary or permanent residence permit is required throughout the whole period, the application is filed in person at the place of residence
language: knowledge of the Croatian language and Latin script (except persons over 60), confirmed by an exam or otherwise
children: children can acquire citizenship together with the naturalizing parent if they hold a residence permit/permanent residence in Croatia or if both parents naturalize at the same time

counts_note: Art. 8 of Montenegro's Citizenship Law requires lawful continuous residence for 10 years before filing. The citizenship-by-investment programme was closed at the end of 2022 and is not in effect for 2026
presence: legal continuous residence is required throughout the entire 10-year period
language: basic command of Montenegrin for oral communication
children: children acquire citizenship if both parents naturalize, or one parent naturalizes and the child lawfully resides with that parent in Montenegro (children over 14 must give consent)

presence: permanent residence under permanent residence status, compliance with the usual presence requirements in the country is required
language: Czech language exam (level B1) and a test on the basics of Czech statehood/history

counts_note: Standard 'carta de nacionalización' requires a minimum of 5 years from the first record of temporary residence (for holders of permanent residency); 'simplified naturalisation' (art. 85 of law 21.325) is possible after 2 years with a Chilean spouse (married for 2+ years) or blood relation to a Chilean up to the 2nd degree
presence: continuous actual residence in the country during the calculation period is required
language: no separate formal Spanish exam is stated in the official source; assessed at an interview
children: children of foreigners can apply from age 14 with notarised parental consent; for younger children, citizenship is usually processed in conjunction with the parent's status

counts_note: Ordinary naturalization requires 10 years of residence in Switzerland and a permanent residence permit (C permit); years lived between ages 8 and 18 count double (relevant for the sample household's children - their path may be shorter than the parent's); a minimum of 6 years of physical presence is mandatory in any case. Time under B/C/Ci permits counts in full, F - by half, N (asylum) and L (short-term) - does not count. In addition, cantons and communes set their own minimum residence periods (2-5 years)
presence: at least 6 years of actual physical presence out of the required 10 (or less with double counting of ages 8-18), plus cantonal/municipal minimums
language: successful integration and command of the national language of the region of residence (level set by the canton, generally oral A2/B1, written A2)
children: for the older child (arriving at an earlier age, hypothetically) a double counting of years between 8 and 18 would apply — that is, the child's own period could be shorter; for the younger child — double counting for the years 8-18 applies likewise

counts_note: The reform enters into force on 6 June 2026: the residence period for naturalization increases from 5 to 8 years, a requirement of self-sufficiency ('self-sufficiency') and proof of good conduct is added; a requirement of knowledge of the Swedish language and society is introduced (previously adults did not need a language test). Important: under the new rules minor children are no longer included automatically in the parent's application - each child must apply individually
presence: permanent residence (hemvist) for 8 years under the new rules
language: under the new rules (from 06.06.2026) — a test of knowledge of the Swedish language and the basics of Swedish society
children: from 06.06.2026 children submit applications individually (not automatically with the parent), which lengthens and complicates the process for the sample household

counts_note: Naturalisation under the classical Ceylon/Sri Lanka Citizenship Act is difficult and in practice rarely available to ordinary foreigners without special merits or marriage to a Sri Lankan citizen; official data on residence periods are fragmentary, need additional verification with the Department of Immigration & Emigration of Sri Lanka
children: no reliable data

counts_note: Ley Orgánica de Movilidad Humana: naturalization through a 'carta de naturalización' requires a minimum of 3 years of continuous legal residence with a permanent visa (for refugees/stateless persons — 2 years). Children are exempt from the language and general exam
presence: continuous legal residence with a permanent visa status for at least 3 years
language: command of Spanish orally and in writing (for adults; graduates of Spanish-language universities of Ecuador, minors and persons with disabilities are exempt)
children: for children under 18, consent of parents/guardians is required; minors are exempt from the language and general exam, their opinion is taken into account

counts_note: Residence in Estonia for 8 years before filing is required, of which at least 5 years on a permanent basis (permanent residence permit/permanent residence)
presence: residence of at least 8 years, of which 5 years on a permanent basis; permanent registration of the place of residence is required
language: Estonian language exam (level B1), those educated in Estonian are exempt

counts_note: The Citizenship Act 1995 requires continuous 'ordinarily resident' residence of at least 5 years IMMEDIATELY BEFORE the application, but for this the applicant must already hold permanent residence, obtaining which itself usually takes years — in total the path to citizenship is estimated at about 10 years (5 years before obtaining permanent residence + 5 years of residence with permanent residence)
presence: continuous actual residence as a permanent resident for at least 5 years immediately before applying
language: sufficient knowledge of one of the official languages of South Africa and understanding of the rights/duties of a citizen
children: the law does not provide for automatic extension of the parent's naturalisation to minor foreign children — their status is determined separately under sections 2-4 of the Act

counts_note: General naturalisation requires at least 5 years of continuous legal residence and a status permitting permanent residence (permanent residence eligible status); simplified periods — 3 years with certain family ties, 2 years in marriage to a Korean citizen (or 3 years of marriage + 1 year of residence)
presence: continuous legal residence of 5 years with the appropriate visa status
language: test of knowledge of the Korean language and society (KIIP or an equivalent naturalisation exam)
children: the official source does not specify; as a rule the status of minor children is tied to the parent's visa status, separate clarification with the Korea Immigration Service is required

counts_note: From 1 April 2026 the residence period for naturalisation was increased from 5 to 10 consecutive years (Ministry of Justice reform announced 27.03.2026, came into force with practically no transition period). All applications not decided by 1 April 2026 are assessed under the new 10-year standard; previously approved applications are not subject to review
presence: 10 consecutive years of residence in Japan before applying (under the new standard from April 2026)
language: command of Japanese at a level sufficient for everyday life (oral exam, a written test of elementary Japanese for school-age children is often not required separately)
children: the official source does not detail the procedure for minors; as a rule children apply together with the naturalizing parent, the transitional rules of the 2026 reform need to be clarified separately
